settings.ai.decisions.enableDesc: Fast typed judgments (classify, route, score) from Jev, TypeSafe's System One model, or a local Laya server. Choose what they are used for under Advanced settings.
settings.ai.decisions.featureAdaptiveThi: Before each turn, Jev/Laya rates how much reasoning your message needs. Simple requests run with a lower thinking level for that turn, saving time and cost; hard ones keep your setting. It never goes above the level you chose. Pushback on the previous reply keeps your level, and requests that change or send something hard to undo get at least high. Your message, the end of the previous reply (1,200 characters) and the names of attached files are sent to the decision model.
settings.ai.decisions.featureAutomationC: Let automations check a yes/no condition before they run.

An automation can carry a condition written as a question, such as "Is the user reporting a bug?". Before the automation starts a session, Jev/Laya answers it from the event and the session's latest messages, and skips the run when the answer is no. Automations without a condition are unaffected.
settings.ai.decisions.featureDecideToolD: Let the agent classify, route and score items with the decide tool. Applies to new sessions.
settings.ai.decisions.featureDecideToolT: The agent can call the decision model (Jev, or Laya on your machine) to classify, route, score or yes/no-check items, for example sorting 200 emails into folders in one call.
settings.ai.decisions.featureGuardedMode: Add a Guarded permission mode that asks before risky actions.

Adds Guarded next to Explore, Ask to Edit and Execute. In Guarded mode the agent works without prompts, but Jev/Laya first checks each command or tool call that is not read-only; if it looks hard to undo, reaches outside the project, or reaches other people or services, you are asked. File edits inside the project run unchecked; edits outside it always ask. Execute mode never asks. If the model does not answer in time, the call runs as in Execute; while this switch or the decision model is off, Guarded behaves like Ask to Edit. Automations and task runs never use it. The command or tool arguments are sent to the decision model.
settings.ai.decisions.featureLargeResult: Keep only the parts of a large tool result the agent needs, instead of summarizing it.

When a tool result is too large for the conversation, it is saved to a file and a small model summarizes it, which takes several seconds. When the agent has said what it is looking for, Jev/Laya picks the parts of the result it needs, and the agent gets those parts and the saved file instead of a summary. Without a clear answer, or when most of the result is needed, it is summarized as before.
settings.ai.decisions.featureMidTurnMess: Decide whether a message sent while the agent works steers it or waits.

When you send a message while the agent is working, Jev/Laya judges whether it corrects the current task (delivered right away) or is a separate follow-up (queued until the task finishes). Queued messages that belong to the same request are sent together as one turn. Without a clear answer the connection's usual behaviour applies.
settings.ai.decisions.featureRiskBadgesD: Tag permission prompts with what the action does.
settings.ai.decisions.featureRiskBadgesT: Before a permission prompt appears, Jev/Laya tags it with what the action does: deletes data, sends data out, publishes, touches secrets, changes the system, or spends money. Informational only: the prompt, its buttons and your choice are unchanged. The prompt's description and command are sent to the decision model.
settings.ai.decisions.featureSemanticLab: Evaluate yes/no auto-apply rules on labels (for example "Is this about billing?") on every message.
Label rules can be yes/no questions such as "Is this about billing?". Jev/Laya answers them for every message you send, and the label is applied when the answer clears the rule's threshold.
settings.ai.decisions.featureSmartTitles: Skip titling small talk and refresh titles when the topic moves on.

When a session starts with small talk such as "hi", Jev/Laya holds the AI title back until you ask for something. Every few messages it also checks whether an automatic title still describes the conversation and refreshes it if not. Titles you set yourself are never changed.
settings.ai.decisions.featureSubagentMod: Run simple subagent tasks on a cheaper model.

Before a Claude subagent starts, Jev/Laya rates its task: searches and lookups run on Haiku, reading and substantial work on Sonnet, and hard reasoning keeps the session's model. It never goes above the session's model and leaves calls that name a model alone. Without a confident answer the Subagent model setting applies. The subagent's task (up to 4,000 characters) is sent to the decision model.
settings.ai.decisions.featureSuggestions: Point the agent at a skill or source your message plainly needs.

Before a message is handled, Jev/Laya compares it with your skills and with sources that are set up but not active in this session. When one clearly fits, the agent gets a hint to use it: read the skill, or activate the source. The decision model never enables anything itself; the agent decides, with the usual permissions. Your message and the names and descriptions of your skills and sources are sent to the decision model.
settings.ai.decisions.featureTaskRepairs: Re-run only the steps a failed check points at.

When a task's verification fails without naming the broken steps, Jev/Laya reads the failure reason and judges which steps it points at. Only those steps and the ones that depend on them are repaired, instead of the whole task. With no clear answer the whole task is repaired, as before.
settings.ai.decisions.featureTaskVerdict: When a task verifier forgets the VERDICT line, read the verdict out of its reply instead of asking again.
When a task verifier's reply has no VERDICT line, Jev/Laya reads it as pass, fail or unclear. Only a confident pass or fail is used; otherwise the verifier is asked again.
settings.ai.decisions.featureTurnOutcome: Flag sessions that need you when a turn ends.

After each turn, Jev/Laya reads the agent's last message and judges whether it finished, needs your input, or got stuck. Open sessions that need you move to Needs Review. In task runs, a step that asks a question or gives up is retried or flagged instead of marked done.

settings.labels.aboutText1: Labels help you organize sessions with colored tags. Use them to categorize conversations by project, topic, or priority — making it easy to filter and find related sessions later.
settings.labels.aboutText2: Each label can optionally carry a value with a specific type (text, number, or date). This turns labels into structured metadata — for example, a "priority" label with value 3, or a "due" label with a date.
settings.labels.aboutText3: Auto-apply rules assign labels automatically when a message matches a regex pattern. For example, pasting a Linear issue URL can auto-tag the session with the project name and issue ID — no manual tagging needed.
settings.labels.autoApplyRulesDesc: Regex patterns that automatically apply labels when matched in user messages. For example, paste a Linear issue URL and automatically tag the session with the project name and issue ID.
settings.labels.labelHierarchyDesc: All labels configured for this workspace. Labels can be nested to form groups.
settings.labels.noLabelsDesc: Labels can be created by the agent or by editing labels/config.json in your workspace.

settings.messaging.lark.instructions:
1. Open Lark Open Platform (lark) or Feishu Open Platform (feishu) and create a Custom App
2. Copy the App ID (cli_…) and App Secret
3. Enable im:message + im:message.group_at_msg + im:message:send_as_bot scopes
4. Subscribe to the im.message.receive_v1 event in long connection mode
5. Leave the Encrypt Key field blank — long connection mode doesn't use payload encryption

settings.permissions.aboutText1: Permissions control how much autonomy your agent has. In Explore mode, the agent can only read and research — perfect for understanding a problem before committing to changes. When you're ready, switch to Execute mode to let the agent implement the plan autonomously.
settings.permissions.aboutText2: A good workflow: start in Explore to let the agent investigate, review the proposed plan, then execute with confidence.
